newsitem.title: USA: USDA July 11 U.S. crop highlights - USDA.
newsitem.headline: USDA July 11 U.S. crop highlights - USDA.

text.p: The U.S. winter wheat harvest will reach 1.781 billion bushels, up 11 percent from last month's forecast and 20 percent above 1996's crop, the Agriculture Department said Friday in its monthly crop report.
USDA said based on July 1 conditions, the U.S. winter wheat yield is forecast at a record high 42.8 bushels per acre, up 3.5 bushels from June 1 and 5.6 bushels per acre above last year.
USDA's forecast exceeded analysts' expectations, which averaged 1.687 billion bushels for the 1997 winter wheat crop. The winter wheat harvest will be largely completed by the end of July.

For all wheat, the USDA estimated production of 2.431 billion bushels, up seven percent from 2.282 billion in 1996. USDA said based on July 1 conditions, the U.S. yield is forecast at 38.3 bushels per acre, up 2.0 bushels from last year, buoyed by an increase in winter wheat production.
Wheat ending stocks for 1997/98 were raised to 650 million bushels, up 71 million bushels from USDA's estimate last month.

The USDA raised its estimate for 1997/98 soybean ending stocks to 285 million bushels, up from 240 million seen in June. Soybean ending stocks for 1996/97 were pegged at 125 million bushels, down from 130 million forecast last month.
With U.S. farmers having planted the largest soybean crop in more than a decade, this year's soybean harvest was projected to hit a record 2.690 billion bushels, USDA said.
The U.S. 1997/98 corn crop was projected at 9.700 billion bushels, down 140 million from last month because of the shift in planted acreage to soybeans.
Corn ending stocks for 1997/98 were cut to 1.196 billion bushels from USDA's previous projection of 1.349 billion bushels.
The new cotton crop was estimated at 18.00 million 480-lb bales, down from 18.50 million estimated in June.
In the USDA's first estimate of the season for barley and oats production based on farmer surveys, USDA pegged the 1997 barley crop at 372 million bushels and pegged oats at 183 million bushels.
